theory.intro: Integrating the acceleration vector componentwise gives velocity, and integrating again gives position. Each integration adds a **vector constant** $\underset{\sim}{c}$, not a single number. Fix the two constants using the given initial velocity and initial position.
facts: Integrate the $\underset{\sim}{i}$ component and the $\underset{\sim}{j}$ component separately.
The constant of integration is a vector $\underset{\sim}{c}=c_{1}\underset{\sim}{i}+c_{2}\underset{\sim}{j}$, so each component gets its own constant.
Substituting the initial velocity into the general velocity gives both components of the first constant.
Substituting the initial position into the general position gives both components of the second constant.

Retain the velocity constant when integrating a second time: it contributes a term proportional to $t$ in the position. Find it using the given velocity condition, either before the second integration or afterwards.
An initial condition may be given at a time other than $t=0$; substitute that time instead.
Check the answer by differentiating it twice and by substituting the given conditions.
steps: Integrate each component of $\underset{\sim}{a}(t)$ and add a vector constant
Use the initial velocity to find that constant, giving $\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$
Integrate each component of $\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$ and add a second vector constant
Use the initial position to find that constant, giving $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)$

workedExamples.question_text: A particle has acceleration $\underset{\sim}{a}(t)=8t\,\underset{\sim}{i}-6\underset{\sim}{j}$ and velocity $\underset{\sim}{v}(0)=3\underset{\sim}{i}+2\underset{\sim}{j}$. Find $\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Integrate each component and add a vector constant.
$\begin{aligned}\underset{\sim}{v}(t)&=4t^{2}\underset{\sim}{i}-6t\,\underset{\sim}{j}+\underset{\sim}{c}\end{aligned}$
Using $\underset{\sim}{v}(0)=3\underset{\sim}{i}+2\underset{\sim}{j}$ gives $\underset{\sim}{c}=3\underset{\sim}{i}+2\underset{\sim}{j}$.
$\begin{aligned}\underset{\sim}{v}(t)&=(4t^{2}+3)\underset{\sim}{i}+(2-6t)\underset{\sim}{j}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: For $t\geq0$, a particle has acceleration $\underset{\sim}{a}(t)=\dfrac{2}{(t+1)^{2}}\underset{\sim}{i}+9\sqrt{t}\,\underset{\sim}{j}$ and velocity $\underset{\sim}{v}(0)=\underset{\sim}{i}-2\underset{\sim}{j}$. Find $\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Write the components as powers and integrate separately.
$\begin{aligned}\underset{\sim}{v}(t)&=\int\left(2(t+1)^{-2}\underset{\sim}{i}+9t^{1/2}\underset{\sim}{j}\right)\,dt\\&=-\frac{2}{t+1}\underset{\sim}{i}+6t^{3/2}\underset{\sim}{j}+c_{1}\underset{\sim}{i}+c_{2}\underset{\sim}{j}\end{aligned}$
Using the velocity at $t=0$:
$\begin{aligned}-2+c_{1}&=1\\c_{1}&=3\\c_{2}&=-2\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\underset{\sim}{v}(t)&=\left(3-\frac{2}{t+1}\right)\underset{\sim}{i}+(6t^{3/2}-2)\underset{\sim}{j}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: A particle has acceleration $\underset{\sim}{a}(t)=6\underset{\sim}{i}+12t\,\underset{\sim}{j}$, with $\underset{\sim}{v}(0)=-\underset{\sim}{i}+2\underset{\sim}{j}$ and $\underset{\sim}{r}(0)=4\underset{\sim}{i}-3\underset{\sim}{j}$. Find $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)$ and $\underset{\sim}{r}(2)$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Integrate acceleration and use the initial velocity.
$\begin{aligned}\underset{\sim}{v}(t)&=6t\,\underset{\sim}{i}+6t^{2}\underset{\sim}{j}+\underset{\sim}{c}\\\underset{\sim}{c}&=-\underset{\sim}{i}+2\underset{\sim}{j}\\\underset{\sim}{v}(t)&=(6t-1)\underset{\sim}{i}+(6t^{2}+2)\underset{\sim}{j}\end{aligned}$
Integrate velocity, retaining both constant terms.
$\begin{aligned}\underset{\sim}{r}(t)&=(3t^{2}-t)\underset{\sim}{i}+(2t^{3}+2t)\underset{\sim}{j}+\underset{\sim}{d}\\\underset{\sim}{d}&=4\underset{\sim}{i}-3\underset{\sim}{j}\\\underset{\sim}{r}(t)&=(3t^{2}-t+4)\underset{\sim}{i}+(2t^{3}+2t-3)\underset{\sim}{j}\end{aligned}$
Substitute $t=2$ into position.
$\begin{aligned}\underset{\sim}{r}(2)&=(12-2+4)\underset{\sim}{i}+(16+4-3)\underset{\sim}{j}\\&=14\underset{\sim}{i}+17\underset{\sim}{j}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: A particle starts at rest with position vector $2\underset{\sim}{i}+\underset{\sim}{j}$. Its acceleration is $\underset{\sim}{a}(t)=-8\cos 2t\,\underset{\sim}{i}+12\sin 2t\,\underset{\sim}{j}$. Find $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)$ and $\underset{\sim}{r}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Starting at rest means $\underset{\sim}{v}(0)=\underset{\sim}{0}$. Integrate each trigonometric component, dividing by $2$ when reversing the chain rule.
$\begin{aligned}\underset{\sim}{v}(t)&=-4\sin 2t\,\underset{\sim}{i}-6\cos 2t\,\underset{\sim}{j}+\underset{\sim}{c}\\\underset{\sim}{v}(0)&=-6\underset{\sim}{j}+\underset{\sim}{c}=\underset{\sim}{0}\\\underset{\sim}{c}&=6\underset{\sim}{j}\\\underset{\sim}{v}(t)&=-4\sin 2t\,\underset{\sim}{i}+(6-6\cos 2t)\underset{\sim}{j}\end{aligned}$
Integrate again and use the initial position.
$\begin{aligned}\underset{\sim}{r}(t)&=2\cos 2t\,\underset{\sim}{i}+(6t-3\sin 2t)\underset{\sim}{j}+\underset{\sim}{d}\\\underset{\sim}{r}(0)&=2\underset{\sim}{i}+\underset{\sim}{d}=2\underset{\sim}{i}+\underset{\sim}{j}\\\underset{\sim}{d}&=\underset{\sim}{j}\\\underset{\sim}{r}(t)&=2\cos 2t\,\underset{\sim}{i}+(6t-3\sin 2t+1)\underset{\sim}{j}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\underset{\sim}{r}\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)&=2\cos\frac{\pi}{2}\,\underset{\sim}{i}+\left(\frac{3\pi}{2}-3\sin\frac{\pi}{2}+1\right)\underset{\sim}{j}\\&=\left(\frac{3\pi}{2}-2\right)\underset{\sim}{j}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: A particle has acceleration $\underset{\sim}{a}(t)=18e^{3t}\underset{\sim}{i}-4\underset{\sim}{j}$, with $\underset{\sim}{v}(0)=8\underset{\sim}{i}+3\underset{\sim}{j}$ and $\underset{\sim}{r}(0)=5\underset{\sim}{i}-\underset{\sim}{j}$. Find $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Integrate acceleration componentwise.
$\begin{aligned}\underset{\sim}{v}(t)&=6e^{3t}\underset{\sim}{i}-4t\,\underset{\sim}{j}+c_{1}\underset{\sim}{i}+c_{2}\underset{\sim}{j}\end{aligned}$
Using the initial velocity:
$\begin{aligned}6+c_{1}&=8\\c_{1}&=2\\c_{2}&=3\\\underset{\sim}{v}(t)&=(6e^{3t}+2)\underset{\sim}{i}+(3-4t)\underset{\sim}{j}\end{aligned}$
Integrate again.
$\begin{aligned}\underset{\sim}{r}(t)&=(2e^{3t}+2t)\underset{\sim}{i}+(3t-2t^{2})\underset{\sim}{j}+d_{1}\underset{\sim}{i}+d_{2}\underset{\sim}{j}\end{aligned}$
Using the initial position:
$\begin{aligned}2+d_{1}&=5\\d_{1}&=3\\d_{2}&=-1\\\underset{\sim}{r}(t)&=(2e^{3t}+2t+3)\underset{\sim}{i}+(3t-2t^{2}-1)\underset{\sim}{j}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: A particle has acceleration $\underset{\sim}{a}(t)=12t\,\underset{\sim}{i}-6\underset{\sim}{j}$. Given $\underset{\sim}{v}(1)=8\underset{\sim}{i}-2\underset{\sim}{j}$ and $\underset{\sim}{r}(1)=5\underset{\sim}{i}+3\underset{\sim}{j}$, find $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Integrate acceleration.
$\begin{aligned}\underset{\sim}{v}(t)&=6t^{2}\underset{\sim}{i}-6t\,\underset{\sim}{j}+c_{1}\underset{\sim}{i}+c_{2}\underset{\sim}{j}\end{aligned}$
The velocity condition is at $t=1$.
$\begin{aligned}6+c_{1}&=8\\c_{1}&=2\\-6+c_{2}&=-2\\c_{2}&=4\\\underset{\sim}{v}(t)&=(6t^{2}+2)\underset{\sim}{i}+(4-6t)\underset{\sim}{j}\end{aligned}$
Integrate velocity.
$\begin{aligned}\underset{\sim}{r}(t)&=(2t^{3}+2t)\underset{\sim}{i}+(4t-3t^{2})\underset{\sim}{j}+d_{1}\underset{\sim}{i}+d_{2}\underset{\sim}{j}\end{aligned}$
Use the position condition at $t=1$.
$\begin{aligned}2+2+d_{1}&=5\\d_{1}&=1\\4-3+d_{2}&=3\\d_{2}&=2\\\underset{\sim}{r}(t)&=(2t^{3}+2t+1)\underset{\sim}{i}+(4t-3t^{2}+2)\underset{\sim}{j}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: For $t\geq0$, a particle has acceleration $\underset{\sim}{a}(t)=-4\underset{\sim}{j}$. It starts at the origin with velocity $6\underset{\sim}{i}+8\underset{\sim}{j}$. Find its position vector (a) when its velocity is parallel to $\underset{\sim}{i}$ and (b) when it next returns to $y=0$.

mastery.question_text:
A particle has acceleration $\underset{\sim}{a}(t)=6t\,\underset{\sim}{i}-4\underset{\sim}{j}$.
Given that $\underset{\sim}{v}(2)=17\underset{\sim}{i}+\underset{\sim}{j}$ and $\underset{\sim}{r}(2)=16\underset{\sim}{i}+11\underset{\sim}{j}$, find $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)$.

A particle has acceleration $\underset{\sim}{a}(t)=-10\underset{\sim}{j}$, with $\underset{\sim}{v}(0)=18\underset{\sim}{i}+30\underset{\sim}{j}$ and $\underset{\sim}{r}(0)=\underset{\sim}{0}$.
Find the position vector of the particle at the instant it next returns to the level $y=0$.
mastery.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$
$=18\underset{\sim}{i}+(30-10t)\underset{\sim}{j}$
$\underset{\sim}{r}(t)$
$=18t\,\underset{\sim}{i}+(30t-5t^{2})\underset{\sim}{j}$
$30t-5t^{2}=0$
$5t(6-t)=0$
$t=0$ or $t=6$
The particle starts at $t=0$, so it returns when $t=6$.
$\underset{\sim}{r}(6)$
$=108\underset{\sim}{i}+(180-180)\underset{\sim}{j}$
$=108\underset{\sim}{i}$
[tikz]\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]
\begin{axis}[axis lines=middle, xlabel={$x$}, ylabel={$y$}, xmin=-12, xmax=126, ymin=-8, ymax=56, xtick={54,108}, ytick={45}, width=12cm, height=8cm, samples=100, clip=false]
\addplot[thick, domain=0:108] {5*x/3 - 5*x*x/324} node[pos=0.78, above right] {$y=\frac{5x}{3}-\frac{5x^{2}}{324}$};
\addplot[only marks, mark=*, mark size=1.6pt] coordinates {(0,0) (108,0)};
\end{axis}
\end{tikzpicture}[/tikz]
